name: Facet
text: Use a dark theme with a high-contrast accent color for key interactive elements. This keeps the interface visible and lively in low-light screencasts, where dark backgrounds reduce eye strain and make bright accents pop. The trade-off is that some users may prefer a light theme, but for screencasts, visibility and engagement outweigh personal preference.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Dark themes with high-contrast accents still fail users with astigmatism or in bright rooms—glare from screenshots ruins clarity. A light theme with a single muted accent (like slate blue) avoids glare while keeping key elements visible; test both under screencast lighting to settle it.
